items.title: Russia claims 1,246 Ukrainian drones intercepted overnight
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry reported intercepting 1,246 Ukrainian drones overnight. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin separately reported a large-scale drone attack targeting the Moscow region. The figures have not been independently verified.

items.title: Russia reports renewed strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said it struck energy and fuel infrastructure that it claimed supported Ukrainian military operations. It also reported striking a cargo vessel allegedly carrying military supplies. The claims have not been independently verified.

items.title: Russia and North Korea reaffirm economic cooperation
items.summary: Russia and North Korea reportedly signed a protocol following an intergovernmental commission meeting in Pyongyang, reaffirming cooperation in energy, trade, agriculture, education and healthcare.

items.title: Bryansk governor reports nine injured in bus attack
items.summary: Regional authorities attributed an attack on a company employee bus to a Ukrainian drone, reporting nine injuries. The account has not been independently verified.

items.title: Austria reportedly rearrests two Ukrainian intelligence employees
items.summary: Austrian broadcaster ORF reportedly said two Ukrainian military intelligence employees were rearrested on suspicion of espionage. The allegations have not been established in court.

items.title: Emergency electricity outages reported across parts of Kyiv region
items.summary: Ukrainian energy company DTEK reported emergency power outages affecting parts of the Bucha, Fastiv and Obukhiv districts. Separately, local authorities reportedly confirmed a fire at a garage complex in Bila Tserkva.

items.title: Moscow rejects allegations of violating NATO airspace
items.summary: Russia's ambassador to Canada, Oleg Stepanov, rejected allegations that Russia had violated the airspace of NATO member states. The denial represents Moscow's position and does not independently establish the circumstances of the reported incidents.

items.title: Russian diplomat accuses Kyiv of escalating tensions around peace efforts
items.summary: Russian Foreign Ministry ambassador-at-large Rodion Miroshnik alleged that Ukrainian authorities deliberately escalate tensions when diplomatic progress appears possible. His allegation was not independently substantiated in the report.

items.title: Donetsk authorities announce utility information centre
items.summary: Russian-installed regional leader Denis Pushilin announced plans for a centre providing daily updates on water, heating and electricity supplies, including scheduled outages.

items.title: Heating reportedly remains disrupted in Odesa
items.summary: Local media reportedly said that as of November 27, heating had been restored to only slightly more than 400 of approximately 1,000 buildings connected to the city's combined heat and power plant. Efforts to restart electricity generation reportedly continue.

items.title: Horlivka authorities report civilian injury following drone attacks
items.summary: Russian-installed local official Ivan Prikhodko attributed a civilian injury and damage to public facilities and vehicles to Ukrainian drone attacks over the preceding day. The account has not been independently verified.

items.title: Russian-appointed authorities report deadly attack on hospital vehicle
items.summary: The Russian-appointed health ministry in occupied Zaporizhzhia region said a nurse and driver were killed in an alleged Ukrainian drone attack on a Vasylivka hospital vehicle. Two others, including the hospital's chief physician, were reportedly injured. The allegation has not been independently verified.

items.title: Russian security service reports detention over alleged intelligence sharing
items.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service said it detained a resident of occupied Luhansk region on suspicion of passing information about Russian military personnel to Ukraine's security service. The allegations have not been independently verified.

items.title: Libyan foreign minister reportedly seeks compensation from Ukraine
items.summary: Libyan Foreign Minister Abd al-Hadi al-Hweij reportedly said Libya would demand compensation from Ukraine over the reported attack on Benghazi port, including compensation for affected military families and damage to port infrastructure.

items.title: Canada reportedly summons Russian ambassador over missile debris in Poland
items.summary: Canada reportedly summoned Russia's ambassador following the discovery of missile debris in Poland. Its foreign ministry expressed solidarity with NATO allies, warned of unintended escalation and reaffirmed support for Ukraine.

items.title: European satellite manufacturing expansion reported amid push for independent communications
items.summary: A Russian military commentary outlet reported that Aerospacelab opened a satellite manufacturing facility in Belgium supporting the EU's IRIS² secure communications programme. The development comes amid debate over Europe's reliance on external satellite communications providers.
